**Nvidia had the higher fiscal 2026 gross margin, by an estimated ~2.8 percentage points (about 71.1% vs. about 68.3%).** This is an estimate, not a reported figure: I don't have Microsoft's full fiscal 2026 results, and some of Nvidia's figures are from memory. The two fiscal years also cover different periods.

**Nvidia (fiscal 2026, ended January 2026): about 71.1% GAAP gross margin**

| Quarter | Revenue | Gross margin | Gross profit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | $44.1B | 60.5% (cut by the H20 export-restriction charge) | $26.7B |
| Q2 | $46.7B | 72.4% | $33.9B |
| Q3 | $57.0B | 73.4% | $41.9B |
| Q4 | about $68.1B (recalled, not confirmed) | about 75% | about $51.1B |
| **Full year** | **about $215.9B** | **about 71.1%** | **about $153.5B** |

**Microsoft (fiscal 2026, ending June 2026): about 68.3% gross margin**
- Q1 (September 2025): revenue $77.7B, gross margin about 69%.
- Q2 (December 2025): revenue $81.3B, gross margin about 68%.
- Q3 and Q4: I assumed about 68% each, because AI infrastructure spending is weighing on cloud margins.
